title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 26
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 26: honor unfit for fools, the sluggard on his bed, and the whisperer's words.

questions.text: What does this chapter say is not fitting for a fool, like snow in summer?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:1 says like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

questions.text: Why does this chapter say to answer a fool according to his folly?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:5 says answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.

answers.text: Lest he answer you with insults
Lest he be wise in his own eyes

questions.text: What is a fool who repeats his folly compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:11 says as a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.

answers.text: A dog that returns to his vomit
A door turning on its hinges
A thorn bush in a drunkard's hand
A stone bound in a sling

questions.text: For whom is there more hope than for a man wise in his own eyes?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:12 says do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

questions.text: What does the sluggard say is in the road, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:13 says the sluggard says, "There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!"

questions.text: What is the sluggard on his bed compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:14 says as the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.

answers.text: A stone that will not be moved
A log lying in the fire
A dog sleeping in the sun
A door turning on its hinges

questions.text: What is one who meddles in a quarrel not his own compared to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:17 says like one who grabs a dog's ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.

answers.text: One who grabs a dog's ears
One who shoots arrows at random

questions.text: What happens to a quarrel without gossip, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:20 says for lack of wood a fire goes out, and without gossip, a quarrel dies down.

answers.text: It moves to the city gate
It is settled by the lot

questions.text: Why should you not believe a malicious man when his speech is charming?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:25 says when his speech is charming, don't believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart.

answers.text: For his words are like a scorching fire
For he winks his eyes to plot perversities
For there are seven abominations in his heart

questions.text: According to this chapter, what happens to whoever digs a pit?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 26:27 says whoever digs a pit shall fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.

answers.text: He catches the wicked in it
